text:
maya: heads-up — after last night's kernel-selection tweak I see steady resident growth on a box serving long-context chat workloads, seems tied to KV cache reuse across requests.
ashwin: can you paste the profile? which tweak exactly?
maya: switched to the new heuristics that bias for throughput (coarser batching) + fallback to the int8 kernel. noticed GC-like spikes and a growing RSS over ~6h.
olivia: perf-bot just opened an alert -> perf-bot: [alert] KV-cache-memory-growth on gpu-pool-3 (since 03:00 UTC) — regression suspected after 1717590000 deploy.
maya: attaching quick flame output (summaries) — the hotspot is in our cache key path and slab allocator, not the kernel compute itself.
ashwin: maybe key canonicalization changed? we folded session id into the prefix recently.
maya: that's my theory. we've been creating keys with very small differences for continuation tokens. fragmentation looks like many small allocations + few large ones.
lia: any sample of the key gen? small differences make huge coldset footprint.
maya: here's the function snippet we use in runtime (copied):
```
string make_cache_key(Request r) {
  // old: fingerprint(prefix) + tenant
  // new: join(prefix, session_id, seq, normalized_text)
  return fmt::join({fingerprint(r.prefix), r.session, to_string(r.seq), normalize(r.input)}, "#");
}
```
olivia: ah, normalize(r.input) is non-deterministic across callers (we do different whitespace trimming in python vs cpp), that will explode the keyspace.
ashwin: if prefixes differ by a punctuation or trailing space, they won't reuse KV entries -> lots of near-duplicates.
maya: profiler dump (top lines):
- 28% slab alloc
- 17% cache lookup memcpy
- 12% key hash
- 9% eviction scan
- 6% page-copy during compaction
- rest split across batching code
lia: eviction scan at 9% is suspicious — we may be compaction thrashing.
ashwin: do we have eviction events in the logs? maya: yes, from the runtime logs:
```
2026-03-17T03:12:05Z [evict] eviction:start pool=kv age=62MB candidates=2048
2026-03-17T03:12:05Z [evict] moved pages=180 freed=32MB
2026-03-17T03:12:06Z [rehydrate] prefix fq=0.12 reuse=0.04
```
olivia: reuse=0.04 for prefixes, that's low. the frequency suggests we're not coalescing prefixes.
lia: how many distinct prefixes per session? maya: on that box it's ~46k prefixes for ~3k active sessions.
ashwin: yikes, average ~15 prefixes per session — expected. But 46k unique prefixes means fragmentation.
maya: also saw high page-copy during compaction, likely because slab pages are small and many tiny objects.
olivia: two immediate fixes: 1) canonicalize prefixes (trim, unicode normalize, collapse whitespace) before fingerprinting; 2) introduce short-term session-local canonical table to map near-duplicate keys to canonical fingerprint.
lia: suggestion 2 is interesting: session-local interning would collapse duplicates inside a session but cost memory per-session. tradeoff test needed.
ashwin: we should also adjust batching heuristics: coarser batching increased interleaving of requests and made prefix locality worse. switch batching bias to prefer session affinity when longctxs detected.
maya: agree. plan of attack:
- normalize keys upstream (maya)
- add session intern table with limited capacity + LRU (ashwin)
- change batching policy to prefer sticky routing for long contexts (olivia)
- add micro-compaction pause threshold so we don't compaction-thrash (lia)
olivia: i've got a canary branch that reverts the throughput bias and adds a session-affinity flag; running on a small pool now.
maya: test commands I used:
```
./perf/run_kv_workload --sessions=3000 --avg-prefixes=15 --duration=8h --enable-int8-kernel
```
olivia: run that on canary, check reuse ratio and RSS at 1h/4h/8h.
ashwin: also add a differential test where we compare fingerprint counts pre/post-normalize to measure keyspace reduction.
lia: noted. I'll write a microbench for compaction costs (page-copy counts).
perf-bot: [note] linked ticket PR-9287 for regression tracking: https://redwood/internal/pr/9287
maya: quick experiment: locally canonicalizing whitespace dropped unique prefix fingerprints from 46k -> 7.2k on a 1h sample.
olivia: promising. what's the impact on reuse?
maya: reuse ratio went 0.04 -> 0.62 in that sample.
ashwin: that would massively reduce eviction pressure.
lia: still want session-interning as defense. it collapses non-normalizable differences (e.g., tokens that have lost punctuation during tokenization mismatch).
maya: agreed. action owners: maya normalize + experiment results by EOD, ashwin session-intern prototype by tomorrow, olivia rollback-canary if RSS doesn't flatten by 2h, lia compaction microbench by tomorrow.
ashwin: add a metric for "cache_key_variants_per_prefix" to monitor.
olivia: i'll wire it into console dashboard and set a regression alarm at 1.5x baseline.
maya: thanks. one more note — kernel selection still matters: when int8 fallback was used latency dropped but the batching change increased interleaving, so fixes are both keying + routing.
lia: file a follow-up to consider slab-size tuning for small-value density as a mid-term fix.
maya: cool. tagging @eng-runtime for visibility. :thumbsup:
ashwin: thanks, will follow up in PR-9287.
olivia: thanks all.
perf-bot: [automated] thread closed for inactivity after 48h unless new comment added.
